summary.text: A 29-year-old woman with three previous normal pregnancies, no concurrent diseases and no folic acid supplementation presented at 28–29 weeks of gestation in an unmonitored pregnancy with altered general condition, lower abdominal cramps and transient lumbar pain. She had not attended prenatal check-ups, and maternal serum AFP had not been measured at 16 to 18 weeks.

Ultrasound showed a female fetus in pelvic presentation with lumbosacral myelomeningocele, and a decision was made to proceed with caesarean delivery. At birth the newborn weighed 1100 g, had an Apgar score of 1 at one minute, cyanosis, apnea, bradycardia, paralyzed lower limbs and an exposed, uncovered lumbosacral defect about 8 cm by 8 cm. Transfontanelle ultrasound showed severe myelomeningocele, Chiari malformation type II and pronounced hydrocephalus.

The newborn received intubation, chest compressions, mechanical ventilation, epinephrine and a saline bolus; blood gas analysis showed severe mixed and metabolic acidosis. Despite all efforts the newborn died shortly after birth. Anatomopathological and histopathological examination described findings in placenta, cord, brain, lung, liver and kidney; karyotyping could not be performed.

ambiguities.issue: The results paragraph lists lung, liver and kidney histopathological findings for the newborn (unexpanded lung tissue, vascular stasis, thrombosis, hemorrhage, lymphocytic infiltration, stasis, medullary hematic extravasation, vascular thrombosis), whereas the discussion, citing the same slides (Figure 2D, 2E, 2F), says no pulmonary, hepatic or renal abnormalities were identified on histopathological examination. Same subject and same examination. Renal ongoing histodifferentiation is a developmental description, not an abnormality claim, and is not quarantined; the macroscopic atelectasis and organ stasis come from a different (macroscopic) examination and are not quarantined.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not reconcile the statements or decide which is correct; the abnormal lung, liver and kidney histology facts and the discussion statement are review_only.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not treat the two descriptors as one measurement or as a correction of one another; they come from different examinations and are kept as separate facts.

evidence.quote: The delayed diagnosis contributed to the progression of degenerative and traumatic lesions in the neural tissue

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the two actual JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual submission.
Index patient is the 29-year-old woman; fetus and newborn facts are kept in her record with subject fetus or newborn (ROSTER-RELATIVES). Placenta and umbilical cord histology use subject other.

Discussion statement that no pulmonary, hepatic or renal abnormalities were identified on histopathology (same newborn, same slides) conflicts with the listed abnormal lung, liver and kidney histology findings; those findings and the discussion statement are review_only. Renal ongoing histodifferentiation is not an abnormality claim and stays included.
Only the decision to proceed with caesarean delivery is stated; delivery mode is not stated.
Counterfactual and prognostic statements (earlier care could have improved outcomes, folic acid might have prevented the defect, ultrasound indicating a severe prognosis) are not recorded as facts.
Author labels for hyperkalemia (potassium 4.43 mmol/L), hyponatremia and hypocalcemia are kept as the author's words; no reference-range flags were derived.
Literature and cohort statements in the introduction and discussion (prevalence, recurrence risk, trials, fortification) are background and not copied to the patient.

The prognosis phrase "indicating a severe prognosis" and author causal statements ("This condition resulted from an unmonitored pregnancy") are not recorded as facts; the postmortem timing of the anatomopathological examination is not stated, so no relation orders it after death.
